item.title: Fitbit Edge: Premium Design for an Active Life (4 minute read)
item.description: Fitbit Edge pairs the brand's largest, brightest Hybrid OLED tracker display with a tactile side button for quick control mid-workout, even with sweaty fingers. A subtly curved chassis of 100% recycled aluminum keeps sensors against the wrist for 24/7 heart-rate and sleep tracking. Four finishes, four redesigned band styles, and up to seven days of battery life round out the design.

item.title: Windows Security is finally getting the Windows 11 makeover it should've had years ago (2 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft is redesigning Windows Security to finally align its interface with the rest of Windows 11, replacing layouts and visual elements that still feel inherited from an older generation of Windows. Navigation, typography, spacing, colors, controls, dialogs, and status indicators are being modernized, with layouts also adapting more consistently across different window sizes. The update additionally improves how security status and available actions are communicated, while device information on supported managed PCs will progressively load so useful details appear sooner.

item.title: OpenAI now lets you text your ChatGPT Dot agent to get things done (3 minute read)
item.description: ChatGPT Dot can now communicate through iMessage and RCS, letting users assign tasks, send photos or voice notes, and receive proactive updates without opening ChatGPT. Dot can use context from ChatGPT conversations and connected channels to decide where updates belong, while users can specify that only urgent information should arrive by text and approvals still happen inside ChatGPT. The beta is currently limited to ChatGPT Pro users in the US, with one-to-one messaging supported but no group chats, regular phone calls, or FaceTime.

item.title: The System I No Longer Know by Heart (6 minute read)
item.description: Working with AI agents means the author no longer memorizes every detail of the design system they build, a shift that requires making systems legible to LLMs. That knowledge has to move into the system itself, through explicit naming, current documentation, and composition rules, since agents can't rely on informal context or unwritten history. Understanding why the system works still matters, but less inventory in the designer's head is a trade worth taking if the system knows more about itself.

item.title: Building an AI-ready design system library: Code → Figma with MCP. Hands-on guide (15 minute read)
item.description: Figma captures only part of the behavior encoded in production components, leaving AI to invent missing details such as focus order, error states, accessibility behavior, and failure handling when translating designs directly into code. Reversing the workflow makes code the source of truth and Figma its visual mirror, with AI and MCP transferring real tokens, styles, properties, variants, and states from a repository into a usable design library. Storybook provides designers with a visual view of the production system, while explicit documentation of anything that cannot be represented in Figma helps maintain parity instead of allowing invisible differences to accumulate.

item.title: Nobody Asked for the Sparkle Button (13 minute read)
item.description: Products, from note apps to banks, ship the same AI chat panel behind a sparkle icon, often switched on by default and hard to turn off. Big cloud firms are projected to spend more than their cloud revenue on capex, while a cited study found that 95 percent of companies saw no measurable return from generative AI pilots. The fix is to build features with AI, not AI features, and to ask who asked, what it's named after, and whether it survives off by default.

item.title: You Are the Best Artist (1 minute read)
item.description: Art is less about conveying emotion to an audience than about capturing it, since a painter alone in a studio still makes art. Comparing skills with others can help, but becoming a better artist is personal, because nobody can express someone's feelings like they can.

item.title: Designing a skill (5 minute read)
item.description: Agent skills can be treated like apps whose interfaces happen to be written largely through instructions, with both the human invoking the skill and the AI interpreting it acting as users. Building a polished skill requires many familiar design practices, including finding the right form, refining copy, creating a visual system, anticipating repeated use, offering meaningful customization, and testing across different contexts. Precise instructions matter because agents fall back on familiar patterns when given vague directions, making skills a useful place to encode the context, trade-offs, intuition, and taste that individual prompts cannot reliably communicate.

item.title: Bioluminescent Alien Worlds That Will Make You Want to Pack Your Bags for the Cosmos (1 minute read)
item.description: Vancouver-based 3D artist Calder Moore builds bioluminescent forests, glowing flora, towering monoliths, and surreal planetary systems under twilight or starry skies.

item.title: This 3D Artist Achieves Incredible Realism to Breathe Life into Striking Character Designs (1 minute read)
item.description: A smug goblin, an albino demon, an adolescent chimp, and a dark elf showcase the striking realism of Australian 3D artist Tom Newbury.

item.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro comes in 14- and 16-inch sizes, pairing a PROLED XDR display with a Dynamic Island-style cutout and a lighter body. A redesigned hinge keeps the screen steady during touch input, while M5 Pro and M5 Max chips power both models. Prices start at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model, with preorders opening October 30 and availability beginning November 6.

item.title: Google Photos Rolls Out a Customizable Redesign of Your ‘Collections' Tab (3 minute read)
item.description: Google Photos on Android is getting a customizable Collections tab that lets users pin frequently opened collections, hide sections they rarely use, and rearrange the layout. Favorites, Screenshots, and Trash are pinned by default, while albums, people and pets, places, and other categories get carousels that can be hidden or reordered. The update arrives with Google Photos version 7.97 through a server-side switch, with no broader release date announced.

item.title: We're Announcing Genie 4, Our New World Model for Real-Time Interactive Simulation (1 minute read)
item.description: Google's Genie 4, a new world model for real-time interactive simulation, brings more realistic visuals and native audio to generated worlds. Natural-language prompts steer scenes live, from moving the camera to changing the weather or adding characters. Rollout starts with a limited group of trusted testers, with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early-access Gemini API partners coming soon.

item.title: Designing for People with ADHD (9 minute read)
item.description: ADHD affects about 5% of people and stems from differences in how the brain develops focus, planning, and self-regulation. It is not a matter of willpower. Helpful patterns include reminders for unfinished drafts, chunked long forms, gradual disclosure of options, and visible progress, while autoplay and infinite scroll are best avoided. ADHD often overlaps with autism, dyslexia, and anxiety, so designing for it tends to help several groups at once.

item.title: One size doesn't fit all: rethinking “good design” across cultures (9 minute read)
item.description: Ideas such as clarity, simplicity, restraint, and functionality are often treated as universal measures of good design even though they emerged from particular Western histories and cultural contexts. Design traditions excluded from the dominant canon can use decoration, complexity, symbolism, and craft in ways that are deeply functional within their cultures, challenging assumptions that minimalism is inherently more sophisticated or understandable. Evaluating design more broadly requires asking who established prevailing standards of taste, whose histories were documented and taught, and whether a design successfully serves its specific cultural purpose rather than conforming to a supposedly universal aesthetic.

item.title: A select should tell you something (6 minute read)
item.description: Customizable HTML selects can now include previews, secondary information, warnings, and other context that helps people recognize the right option instead of deciphering text labels. Practical examples include showing fonts in their actual typefaces, displaying current local times instead of UTC offsets, aligning delivery prices for comparison, and distinguishing people with identical names by job title and department. The technique progressively enhances the native `select`, so unsupported browsers can retain familiar controls while richer desktop experiences provide more useful information without replacing built-in semantics and keyboard behavior.

item.title: Animated Architecture Diagrams from Plain Text (Website)
item.description: Declare semantic nodes, flows, and timed beats in reviewable text. Markdy compiles browser-native motion graphics that stay version-controlled, PR-friendly, and AI-native.

item.title: Open-Source CAD for AI Agents (Website)
item.description: The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models as STEP, GLB, STL, or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks, generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal, and CNC fabrication services.

item.title: Make Wild Visual Effects in Your Browser (Website)
item.description: Ladybug is an effects studio for pictures, video, type, and sound.

item.title: The Software Factory Forgot About Design (4 minute read)
item.description: A four-station workflow of Linear, Paper, a coding agent, and review brings design into the software factory, where issues otherwise turn straight into pull requests. Linear holds the intent, Paper hosts agent-drafted HTML and CSS designs made before implementation, and the coding agent builds from both issue and design. Review checks the build against intent, but agents still lack the history behind decisions, such as past designs, analytics, and design-system reasoning.

item.title: The New York Times turns 175 with an identity, events and a campaign (6 minute read)
item.description: The New York Times is marking its 175th anniversary with a visual identity, campaign, and program of events that use the publication's history as material rather than simply commemorating its age. Familiar elements from its editorial and typographic heritage are reframed across contemporary applications, connecting decades of journalism with the publication's current cultural role. The system demonstrates how an established institution can celebrate recognizable brand equity while giving historical assets new relevance instead of replacing them.

item.title: How Mother Design turned a séance into a new identity for Purple Garden (6 minute read)
item.description: Mother Design began Purple Garden's rebrand with a séance, chakra reading, and automatic drawing workshop, using the resulting forms and feelings to build an identity around spirituality as “A Living Practice.” A whimsical wordmark, crystal-like guidance glyph, warm purple palette, tactile imagery, living typography inspired by cymatic patterns, and expressive motion create an immersive system without relying on familiar psychic-industry clichés. The process moved between physical experimentation, traditional design software, and AI tools, deliberately introducing unpredictability into both the creative process and the finished identity.

item.title: This Creative Agency's Website is Giving Me Tumblr 2000s Vibes, and I'm Here for It (3 minute read)
item.description: Denver's Bound Agency has a handmade, scrapbook-style site by Wunder Werkz that evokes 2000s Tumblr, with a handwritten logo, doodled icons, and tarot cards.

item.title: struggle together (5 minute read)
item.description: AI can remove much of the difficulty involved in learning and making things, but some of that struggle builds judgment, understanding, relationships, and the ability to create things with other people that none could have made alone.

item.title: Stefan Sagmeister's Artworks Turn Global Data into Good News at La Gaîté Lyrique (4 minute read)
item.description: Stefan Sagmeister's solo show "Finally, Something Good" at La Gaîté Lyrique turns UN and World Bank data into artworks arguing that health, democracy, and equality have improved.

item.title: New report slams Microsoft for leveraging dark patterns to force people to use Edge (4 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft continues using dark patterns, including misleading banners, default-browser restrictions, and forced actions, to steer Windows users toward Edge. Users outside the European Economic Area encounter more interference when downloading, setting, and keeping an alternative default browser, demonstrating how regulatory requirements can directly affect interface design. Windows features such as Search and Widgets can also bypass a user's chosen default and open links in Edge, reinforcing concerns that Microsoft's design decisions undermine meaningful browser choice.

item.title: Franki Branding: Inside Koto's New Identity (3 minute read)
item.description: Koto's identity for restaurant discovery app Franki turns finding places to eat into the visual language of an insider's club, centered on bright yellow, oversized rounded typography, candid photography, and conversational copy. Diatype Rounded and a soft geometric symbol create a friendly foundation, while phrases such as “If we know, you know” reinforce Franki's positioning as a knowledgeable friend rather than a conventional recommendation platform. Motion extends through typography, UI, and content to suit the video-first product, while the same system carries into Franki Social Club and physical experiences.

item.title: Access Video and Image Models from Figma Weave via the Figma MCP (1 minute read)
item.description: Figma Weave's full lineup of video and image models, including Seedance, Kling, and Nano Banana, can now be used inside external AI agents through the Figma MCP. Users need a Figma Weave account connected to their Figma account to generate media mid-conversation. Each video or image generated with a Weave model consumes Weave credits.

item.title: 3 design principles in the AI age (5 minute read)
item.description: Three enduring principles remain essential to good design despite AI dramatically accelerating creative work: iteration, feedback, and connecting the dots. Faster generation makes exploring alternatives cheaper, but quality still requires repeated refinement, diverse human perspectives, and judgment about which feedback matters rather than accepting AI's first answer or treating it as the only critic. Designers also need time away from production to process accumulated knowledge and recognize larger connections, because AI can generate faster than humans can meaningfully reflect.

item.title: Design as a garden (2 minute read)
item.description: Creative work can be approached like tending a garden: cultivate favorable conditions, return consistently, encourage unexpected cross-pollination, and protect fragile ideas before judging them too quickly. Pruning unnecessary work and deliberately leaving room for play can be as important as producing more, while not every experiment needs an obvious payoff. Ideas also benefit from periods of inactivity and patience, making it useful to distinguish between moments that require greater effort and those that simply require more time.

item.title: Microsoft's identity for Copilot positions it as a tool for work (7 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft's evolving Copilot identity positions AI as a practical tool embedded in everyday work rather than an abstract futuristic technology. Its animated two-part mark, paired sans-serif and serif typography, gradients, and flexible graphic system create continuity across Microsoft's ecosystem while giving Copilot a recognizable presence of its own. The system is designed to scale across product interfaces, campaigns, and motion, balancing the expressiveness needed to represent generative AI with the clarity expected from a productivity tool.

item.title: Nine Checks Before Shipping a Product Email: A Workflow for Developers and Designers (7 minute read)
item.description: A product email can look right in a design file yet fail its reader through a vanishing action, a surviving staging link, or a duplicate send. Using a workspace invitation as the example, nine checks cover the message's behavioral contract, client compatibility, accessibility, captured application output, link validation, and retry handling. Delivery evidence, such as authentication and bounce handling, is reviewed separately after the template passes.

item.title: Estonian Street Artist is Transforming Ordinary City Walls into Bizarre, Cartoonish Masterpieces (1 minute read)
item.description: Estonian designer and street artist Ingmar Järve, known as Gutface, fills murals, prints, and digital work with distorted figures, deadpan faces, and satirical cartoon humor.

item.title: Apple exploring fix for Safari's cramped layout on the iPhone Duo's outer display (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple is exploring ways for websites to extend into the space behind Safari's right-aligned controls on the iPhone Duo's outer display, potentially giving web designers more usable width without obscuring important content.

item.title: How Do You Create a Design to Last for 1,000 Years? (2 minute read)
item.description: Nebbia's Interlude, a climbable stone portal on a cliff overlooking Lake Whakatipu, is the second completed work in Paererewā's plan for 1,000 works lasting 1,000 years.

item.title: Figma Adds Enterprise AI Credit Controls and Admin APIs (1 minute read)
item.description: Enterprise admins in Figma can now set default paid AI credit access per user, choosing a monthly limit, full access, or none across organizations or billing groups. The limits cover purchased credits only and reserve nothing, so shared pools can still run dry. New admin REST APIs for teams, folders, and files, plus a block on employees opening Starter or Professional plans with company emails, round out the update.

item.title: Apple unveils all-new iPad mini: OLED, thinner design, more (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple's biggest iPad mini update yet introduces a slightly larger 8.5-inch OLED display with 24% thinner bezels, up to 1,200 nits of peak brightness, and an optional nano-texture finish. The 5.4mm-thick design adds IP67 water and dust resistance, an A20 Pro chip, a landscape 12MP Center Stage camera, Acoustic Display audio, faster connectivity, and fast charging. Pre-orders begin October 28 ahead of a November 6 release, with pricing starting at $699 for 128GB.

item.title: These clever apps show off the iPhone Duo's potential (9 minute read)
item.description: Developers are creating playful apps built around the iPhone Duo's folding design. Deck-Man turns albums into virtual cassettes, letting users load a tape with the phone open and close it to listen, complete with mechanical playback sounds. TypeDraw uses the fold as a notebook cover, with customizable paper, drawing tools, and fonts based on the user's handwriting.

item.title: Entering Atomic Design from the screen (10 minute read)
item.description: Atomic Design does not have to begin with small reusable components and work upward, as product teams can instead start with complete screens and discover their underlying structure from user behavior. A scope-first approach identifies what users can do, determines which data or interface region each action affects, and assigns responsibility for that logic before defining components. This helps reveal relationships that a simple interface inventory misses, producing components and templates based on behavioral boundaries rather than visual proximity alone.

item.title: How to Put Your Design System to Work with the Figma Agent (5 minute read)
item.description: A connected design library gives the Figma agent approved components and tokens, while guidelines attached to it encode rules, exceptions, and which variant to pick. Examples on an Examples page or attached to a prompt show how pieces combine, and reusable skills like a /design-system-audit handle repeat processes. Recurring agent mistakes signal that guidelines, library, or examples need updating.

item.title: AI UI Design Prompts: Describe the Interface You Want (10 minute read)
item.description: AI coding tools produce more distinctive interfaces when prompts describe not only a broad visual style but also typography, layout, hierarchy, density, colors, borders, and how specific interface regions should relate to each other. Applying Swiss-inspired, editorial, developer-workbench, and neo-brutalist directions to the same test-results viewer demonstrates how identical functionality can produce radically different compositions while preserving content and behavior. Effective iteration comes from evaluating the rendered interface against the task, then giving concrete feedback about problems such as oversized headings, misplaced controls, or wasted space rather than relying on vague aesthetic instructions.

item.title: Options are expensive. Not having them has a cost too (3 minute read)
item.description: Oxygen is adding a setting that lets KDE users choose between symbolic and colorful action icons, but supporting that seemingly simple preference requires redrawing hundreds of icons individually at multiple sizes. Different pixel dimensions require distinct proportions and levels of detail rather than straightforward scaling, turning one interface option into thousands of assets that must be designed, tested, and maintained. User choice carries a substantial hidden cost, but removing choice also has consequences when people have different visual preferences, habits, and accessibility needs.

item.title: Conran Design Group rebrands luxury accommodation provider Cheval (4 minute read)
item.description: Conran Design Group has repositioned luxury accommodation provider Cheval around “Generous by design,” shifting the brand from a product-led proposition toward experiences defined by space, time, and attention. A new elongated C containing two horses references Cheval's Knightsbridge origins, while Season typography, deep teal, bespoke property emblems, and flag-inspired signage replace more generic black, white, and gold luxury conventions. The flexible identity supports Cheval's expansion across serviced apartments and branded residences while giving individual properties room to express their distinct locations and character.

item.title: Masani Pizza's identity celebrates the family that owns it (5 minute read)
item.description: Saint-Urbain built Masani Pizza's identity around the personality and family behind the restaurant, giving the brand a warm, characterful presence rather than relying on familiar Italian restaurant conventions. Expressive typography, illustrations, photography, and playful graphic details create a visual language that feels personal and rooted in the people running the business. The resulting system turns family character and hospitality into the restaurant's primary point of distinction across packaging, signage, merchandise, and other touchpoints.

item.title: Teenage Engineering is a Masterclass in Product Design (2 minute read)
item.description: Teenage Engineering's music gear pairs aluminum bodies, clearly labeled controls, and purposeful color with a consistent visual language across hardware and software.

item.title: Talented Digital Illustrator Creates Breathtaking, Solitary Worlds That Will Make You Want to Pause and Get Lost in Quiet Reflection (1 minute read)
item.description: Nishanul Nishat paints lone figures in vast, dreamlike landscapes, using soft color palettes and rich lighting to build atmospheric, narrative-driven scenes of quiet solitude.

item.title: The Ambitious EA Sports Rebrand Looks Great from Every Angle (2 minute read)
item.description: DixonBaxi has rebranded EAFC27, turning the triangular cursor logo adopted after the 2023 split from FIFA into a free-form shape that changes with context. The studio behind the F1 and Roblox identities left TV sports conventions behind for a look closer to TikTok and Twitch. The system is built to move from campaign to culture, letting players of every playstyle, age, and background make the brand their own.

item.title: Canva enters the AI image generation race with Craft, and it's thinking beyond pretty pictures (2 minute read)
item.description: Canva Craft is the company's first in-house image generation model. Built specifically for design work such as posters, presentations, social graphics, and other layouts where accurate text and composition matter, its two-stage process first plans object placement, scale, hierarchy, and typography before generating images at up to 2K resolution across 30 aspect ratios, with Magic Layers able to convert results into editable designs. Trained on millions of human-created Canva templates, Craft is available through Dream Lab and Canva's API, with integrations for AI assistants and faster Craft variants also planned.

item.title: Some iPhone Duo displays are cracking, seemingly all in the same way (2 minute read)
item.description: Some iPhone Duo owners are reporting inner displays cracking along the center hinge, typically accompanied by a horizontal block of pixels stuck glowing white. Around ten separate cases have surfaced so far, sometimes during initial setup, with a defective or misaligned hinge component emerging as one possible explanation. Most affected Apple Store customers appear to have received replacements, and the small number of reports means it remains unclear whether this represents a broader hardware problem.

item.title: Your Product is Not the Center of the Universe (4 minute read)
item.description: Established products still assume they sit at the center of users' workflows, a model nearing its end as personal agents work across many tools at once. In its place, products show up wherever the user's agent works, expose their capabilities to any agent, and rely on its memory. In-conversation UI, domain expertise, proprietary data, and fulfillment like hosting, shipping, and payments keep them from becoming commodities.

item.title: Websites Should Be Printable (3 minute read)
item.description: Websites containing substantial text can provide a much better printed experience with a relatively small set of dedicated CSS rules. Print styles can remove navigation, introduce print-only information, resize typography, adapt code blocks, and turn colored links black so pages work better on paper. Supporting printing may be a niche requirement, but it reflects a broader approach to good software in which small, thoughtful accommodations give users more ways to experience content.

item.title: Half my design system metrics don't work anymore (7 minute read)
item.description: Traditional design system metrics such as total component counts, downloads, MCP calls, and self-reported agent success reveal little about whether a system actually produces better work. More useful measures include conformance, accessibility, design-code parity, hard-coded values, component friction, agent adherence, cost per shippable output, and how quickly humans and agents can successfully build with the system. As AI agents become design system users, teams also need repeatable evals that give models real tasks and score their output against intended design principles, implementation rules, and visual quality.

item.title: Everyone is Starting Over (5 minute read)
item.description: Designers at every career stage are effectively starting over, as tools, expectations, and team structures shift fast enough to turn old strengths into liabilities. Reinvention is a habit that demands tolerance for embarrassment. Critical thinking is its counterweight - test each new idea so openness to change never means becoming easy to fool.

item.title: Font pairings 2026: we checked the fonts on 2,190 websites designers loved. Most of them used just one (12 minute read)
item.description: An analysis of 2,190 design-gallery websites found that 60% use the same typeface for headlines and body copy, relying on differences in scale, spacing, and weight rather than traditional font pairings. Among the 871 sites using two families, there were 811 different combinations, while Inter was the most common overall typeface, PP Neue Montreal led paid options, and monospace fonts frequently appeared as a third family for labels and small text. The data suggests contemporary web typography is increasingly defined by craft within a small number of families, with regular-weight, tightly tracked large headlines and carefully controlled spacing doing more visual work than elaborate pairings.

item.title: East Surrey Council reveals in-house brand identity ahead of 2027 launch (3 minute read)
item.description: East Surrey Council's new identity was developed entirely in-house by designers from six local authorities at no additional cost to taxpayers ahead of the authority's April 2027 launch. The selected mark uses layered leaf-like forms to reference the region's contours and countryside while hiding a lowercase “e,” with colors representing woodland, countryside, community, waterways, and heritage, and Lexend providing accessible primary typography. The identity will be introduced gradually as existing signage, vehicles, and other assets reach scheduled replacement points, minimizing waste and transition costs.

item.title: How Lufthansa Systems Prototypes Realistic Maps for the Cockpit with Figma Make (7 minute read)
item.description: Lufthansa Systems now prototypes the dynamic cockpit maps in its Lido Pilot Apps with Figma Make, after static screens failed to feel real to pilots.

item.title: Intent design system (2 minute read)
item.description: Intent's live design system documents its evolving visual language across logos, motion, colors, typography, iconography, and interactive components.

item.title: Apple Music is hiding the original iPod as an easter egg, and there's a secret game too (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple Music is celebrating the iPod's 25th anniversary by turning its website's 404 page into a functional original iPod complete with a click wheel, song previews, settings, and a hidden playable version of the classic Brick game.

item.title: ChatGPT Slides has Shipped, but on Windows 10 the Desktop App Gives You a PowerPoint File (3 minute read)
item.description: ChatGPT Slides began rolling out on October 16 to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users with Space access, but the Windows 10 desktop app provides a PowerPoint file instead of a collaborative deck. Decks live inside Space and inherit its view-and-edit sharing, with ChatGPT joining in when @mentioned like a colleague. Exports reach PowerPoint, PDF, or Google Slides, while Free, Go, and Plus plans still have no release date.

item.title: Google Search Tests Layout Change For Local Knowledge Panel (1 minute read)
item.description: Google is testing a redesigned local knowledge panel that moves the business name, rating, description, and action buttons above the photos, bringing desktop results closer to the existing mobile design. The lower section has also been tightened to create a more compact overall layout. The changes are subtle but could affect how prominently actions such as calls, directions, and website visits appear to searchers.

item.title: Apple's ‘Designers of Tomorrow' highlights creative projects from emerging designers (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple and Design Miami's second Designers of Tomorrow showcase features work from Salem S. Charabi, Isabel Rower, Yoonjeong Lee, and Parafernalia centered on the theme of presence. Their projects explore how physical objects can capture attention and shape experiences, ranging from lighting and furniture to pieces designed for shared interaction. Apple devices are integrated throughout their creative processes, including MacBook Pro for 3D modeling, iPad Pro and Apple Pencil for sketching, and iPhone, Procreate, FaceTime, and iCloud for documenting and collaborating remotely.

item.title: Design System Foundations (2 minute read)
item.description: Any team producing designed outputs already has a design system, which turns the work into incremental improvement rather than a build from zero. Before excitement takes over, everyone needs to agree whether the system means a component library, a shared Figma file, or documentation. Starting with color and typography distilled from existing practice gives guardrails, not straitjackets, and avoids the objections that come with imposed rules.

item.title: A founder with a tool is not a founder with a clue (22 minute read)
item.description: AI has dramatically lowered the cost of producing software, allowing solo founders to handle work that previously required designers, engineers, and other specialists, but easier production does not automatically provide the expertise required to judge whether the result is good. Product quality still depends on hard-earned understanding of users, trust, interaction, strategy, and countless subtle decisions that generative tools can execute without truly evaluating. Small AI-enabled teams can be extraordinarily effective, but treating specialist expertise as unnecessary confuses the ability to make something with the ability to recognize, shape, and refine something worth making.

item.title: Don't Prompt AI. Delegate to It (4 minute read)
item.description: Prompting is fading as a personal skill, and a weekend-built Jira and Confluence briefing agent shows the alternative: letting AI write the prompt while a human defines what good looks like. Four or five rewrite rounds produced a prompt that groups tickets by business topic, flags unverifiable claims, and obeys one key line: do not invent facts. Research backs the approach, with LLM-written instructions matching or beating human ones on 19 of 24 tasks in the 2022 APE paper.

item.description: PixyCAD gives you direct, hands-on editing tools that let you reshape solid models without rebuilding from scratch.

item.title: Review AI-Generated UI Changes with Storybook and Chromatic (8 minute read)
item.description: Sprawling AI-generated UI changesets can pass linting yet render broken layouts, which makes raw diff review structurally inadequate. A four-step playbook scopes each prompt to a single component, isolates changes in Storybook, automates visual regression with Chromatic, and adds a PR checklist. Together they close the gap between code that compiles and code that renders correctly.

item.title: Debunking AI Agent Accessibility Claims and Solving AI Alignment for Accessibility (7 minute read)
item.description: Agents routinely claim work they never did, and having one agent validate another is like letting the fox guard the henhouse. Deque's report found that 88 percent of engineering leaders trust their AI-generated code is accessible, while 64 percent cite accessibility as a top driver of rework. A deterministic harness asking AI only narrow yes-or-no questions creates proof-of-work records for human verification, with Deque reporting that a 30-to-45-minute keyboard test can take seconds.

item.title: The State of Typography in Design Systems (8 minute read)
item.description: A survey of 94 UX and product designers found that 78% can easily change or suggest fonts, while brand alignment is the leading consideration when choosing typefaces, followed by accessibility. Most design systems use fewer than 10 typographic styles, potentially too few to cover common needs, while token adoption remains inconsistent and decisions about typography are rarely revisited after implementation. Scaling type across screen sizes and choosing appropriate styles emerged as the biggest challenges, alongside maintaining cross-platform consistency and getting developers and stakeholders to support better typographic decisions.

item.title: For a brief generation or two, we clicked (2 minute read)
item.description: Graphical interfaces made clicking and tapping a temporary language humans had to learn to communicate with computers, while conversational AI may return interaction to the far older and more natural behavior of simply saying what we want.

item.title: The Senior Art Director Behind Assassin's Creed's Visual Identity Shares His Personal Sketches (1 minute read)
item.description: Montreal art director Raphaël Lacoste, who shaped Assassin's Creed's visual identity at Ubisoft, shares personal sketches and monumental landscape paintings that echo 19th-century Romantic painters like Caspar David Friedrich.

item.title: iPhone Duo orders limited to two per customer as Apple tackles scalping (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple is limiting iPhone Duo purchases to two per customer across markets including the US, UK, Japan, and Spain after shipping dates quickly slipped into January 2027. The restriction applies regardless of configuration and appears designed to reduce scalping, with resellers already listing devices for more than $5,000. Purchase limits cannot eliminate organized scalping entirely, but they could make bulk buying more difficult and improve availability for regular customers.

item.title: Figma co-founder Dylan Field thinks MCP is not a perfect protocol (2 minute read)
item.description: Figma is adding 20 MCP partners even as co-founder Dylan Field argues that the protocol favors frontier AI labs and needs improvement. He says the company wants people to use their Figma data but must limit exposure to reduce potential abuse. Field also pointed to unequal sharing of context across platforms and said Figma plans to support the open-source tool Pi.

item.title: Bluesky Expands its AI-Powered Attie App to Let Anyone Build Websites, Games, and More (2 minute read)
item.description: Bluesky's experimental Attie platform now lets everyday users build websites, quizzes, games, and polls, experiences that previously only software developers could make. CEO Toni Schneider calls it "social vibe coding," with creations tied to ATProto identities and able to reach Bluesky's 47 million registered users. Support for private data, the top developer request, is in alpha with a rollout planned by year's end.

item.title: Top Accessibility Errors in Production and How to Avoid Them (10 minute read)
item.description: Almost 96% of the top million home pages fail at least one automated accessibility check, and the same errors have led WebAIM's report for seven years. Low contrast, missing alt text, unlabeled inputs, and empty links and buttons top the list, each fixable without a rebuild. Automated scans catch only about 30 to 40 percent of issues, so keyboard and screen reader testing still has to happen before release.

item.title: “You've already proof-tested the answer for years” (4 minute read)
item.description: A formal design degree is not necessarily required to build a successful creative career when years of experience, skills, self-study, and leadership already demonstrate professional ability. The 70-20-10 learning model suggests that most professional development comes from practical experience and relationships, with formal education accounting for a relatively small portion. Structured courses can still be valuable when they address a specific knowledge gap, build confidence, or support a desired career direction rather than simply validating an already proven career.

item.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era (8 minute read)
item.description: Treating UI as a pure function of state lets developers see how a screen varies across roles, plans, billing statuses, and flags, which matters more now that agents take on front-end implementation work. In a worked example, an agent that tested only an owner account reported success on a delete action, yet viewers still saw the button despite a “View only” header. Rendering every state combination side by side exposes such gaps, so teams should make display-relevant state explicit and ask what an agent actually checked before merging.

item.title: This Study Measured the Design Choices Behind a Year of Live Ads – Here's What Actually Works (Sponsor)

item.title: HAL Casino is a single-weight serif, sans and mono (3 minute read)
item.description: HAL Typefaces' HAL Casino combines serif, sans, and monospaced styles within a single-weight family, allowing contrasting typographic voices to work together as one system. Its forms draw on historical serif designs and expressive swash lettering while balancing expressive details with enough consistency for the styles to be mixed freely. The result gives designers multiple distinct textures without requiring them to leave a single coordinated type family.

item.title: Digital Accessibility Laws for UX Designers: Which Rules Apply to Your Products (9 minute read)
item.description: Following accessibility best practices doesn't guarantee legal compliance, and the rules differ across the US, UK, and EU. A four-question check covering market, provider, product type, and exemptions helps identify which of the ADA, Section 508, the European Accessibility Act, and UK laws may apply. Cases involving Domino's, Target, and Fashion Nova show the legal and commercial cost of ignoring them.

item.title: Does brand design have a longevity problem? (8 minute read)
item.description: Brands increasingly chase launch-day novelty and short-lived visual trends at the expense of accumulated recognition and long-term usefulness. Durable identities instead build on principles, flexible systems, typography, proportion, composition, and other foundational elements that can evolve without abandoning the equity they have accumulated. Longevity does not require brands to remain visually static, but to preserve their core ideas while adapting their expression to new contexts over decades.

item.title: The Hardest Part of Moving from UX to Hardware is Committing (6 minute read)
item.description: Hardware demands earlier commitment than software, since a released physical product can't be fixed with an update and design choices become costly to reverse.
